The Finlay paddock is one that I believe is important that we return an isolated parcel of land to one that can be a useful addition to our bushland, and that would require some recharacterisation of that. And the staff member at the briefing indicated that that was more than feasible to do that. So, I think that would be an important attribute to add back into our bushland. E10, again, fencing, and 176, 168 are about fencing. I think fencing would be intrusive and not inclusive in terms of being able to enjoy what is currently an open parkland. And getting down to the top points, I just have to refer back to where that is in the document. E18, yep. And coming down to the substantive one, which is PDF L32 on page 192. I'd like to sort of talk about that in some detail. In making these changes or amendments to the plan, I've used some guiding principles behind my decision to submit these amendments, and they are, I fully support the need for, and it is indisputable, the need to have additional sporting facilities in Boronia Park. Boronia Park is a local facility, not a regional one, and should represent that scale. I also believe in, as a guiding principle, Boronia Park is a diverse array of user groups, and all opinions need to be considered. Respect the outcomes of the community consultation process that has been extensive, be an evidence-based and fit-for-purpose decision-making, what is feasible based on need, funding and context of the park, and be respectful of the unique attributes of the heritage of the park. And I see those as the key guiding principles in making decisions, which underlie the amendments which I've put on the table. I've been a strong supporter for many years of improving facilities in Boronia Park. As a resident, I've spoken passionately in favour of facilities when previously planned and considered by the council in 2015. We need to be mindful that plans are not set in stone and do get reviewed regularly. The perception that there is a polarisation of opinion from consult, from the consultation process and the extensive emails I've received, everyone is fierce agreement about improving. There's nobody that says we don't need to improve the facilities. It's a location and scale issue, and I would be very disappointed if people represent me and the community as being something that's opposing additional facilities, because that's just not true. Boronia Park is a local facility, not a regional facility, and should represent that scale. I would be horrified to find, and I'm sure the sporting community, the Huntersville community, if we were to lose control of these facilities to a regional process where clubs out of area and sports that aren't currently played in that area would take a fairly role in using those. It should be at a club level, and the basis of my discussion and my points here is all around a club level. It's a proud club tradition of 122 years, and I believe strongly that 525 square metres that's in the report or in the plan is far excessive. We need to take seriously the findings of the consultation process and as conducted by the independent consultant. So why, after 14 months of consultation, has this process been basically disregarded? Why has the consultant's report, in particular Recommendation 1, been changed significantly following the council briefing a few weeks ago? It is unreasonable, I believe, to alter the report without justification and notification to councillors and justify these changes. This raises a critical issue of the conducting of secret briefings without the transparent public. The public remain unaware of the previous position presented by the consultant and why have they changed their report to dismiss the community concern regarding Option 1 in favour of Option 3. As a compromise, I'm proposing Option 4 as a preferred site. The sporting facility is to be fit for scale and consider materials and context and location. Footplate should not exceed 350 square metres and that complies with the peak bodies, both rugby and cricket, in terms of club-based facilities of this nature. It also aligns very closely with what the proposal originally put on the table by the Hunters of Rugby Club, which was 300 square metres for the building footprint, plus another 100 square metres for a balcony, which was a lightweight sort of structure. The lower floor, as we've all seen, should be all about change rooms, all those facilities that people may need. It should not exceed 6.6 metres in total height and it should easily fit with minimal disturbance between the existing—minimal external disturbance in its locations. Materials should be lightweight, such as weatherboard, corrugation, iron and whatever. A 525 square metre building would resemble the Town Hall or the Des Moines Park facility.

text: Councillor CUMMING. Thank you, Mr Mayor, for the opportunity. It's an important issue and I think these points need to be made. The problem with placing it where it's in the plan at the moment is clearly one that it can't fit. It would end up being a long linear building that would fit—would serve no real purpose functionally and it would provide a very solid block when viewed across the parkland area. It is one that I think it's an important issue to make sure that the heritage of the site is respected and it is a heritage site. We have the grandstand and the curtilage of the oval that is quite crucial in terms of maintaining the long-term context of which that heritage status. It also is important to make sure the scale doesn't intrude on the playing space on Oval 2 and certainly doesn't intrude onto the Oval 1. So a more functional building that would provide the necessary requirements to meet the clubs and the sporting community and the schools that want to use the storage and everybody else is appropriate. We've got the problem also that I feel from reading the probably hundreds of emails that we've got that there is a perception that we're talking about Site 2. That is not the case. A lot of the presentations to Council was about between the car park, the netball courts and Oval 1 and 2. Now that is not the site that Council is proposing in the plan. The site is a very narrow point between the two ovals. Site 4, which is down towards the netball courts, would provide the same amenity, provide the same proximity and more proximity to Oval 3 and I think that is a much more appropriate location. The footprint of the building could be such that it is a block form rather than a long ribbon. If it's at a lower scale it provides that important aspect of not presenting a block in the sight lines across the precinct. So it is crucial that we take into account those aspects that make the park important, particularly in terms of the location of this building and the scale of the building. I think it's equally incumbent on Council to make sure that in doing that it articulates enough detail to allow the approval process to reflect on what the community values are at this location and what has been done through the community consultation. It will be approved by the local planning panel. If we just leave the thing open without giving any guidance then we will end up with something that we'll all regret into the future and if we do go ahead with the current location and you go through the planning process I'm confident that we will find out that it won't fit in that location and then we'll have to go back through another planning process, another consultation process to end up with an outcome and that would take another 18 months. So I think we have to be very serious about what this building will look like, how it will fit in and more importantly whether the location can take what is being proposed and I believe it can't and I fear that if we get down the next level of planning that will be demonstrated and we'll have to go back through another process of developing a plan that has a location that reflects the need. Now I would be suggesting that we both we have a bet each way and if it doesn't turn out that location four near the tennis courts, sorry the cricket nets, then we need to move to option one which is the one that was favoured by the community. Nobody's going to be happy I guess in the outcome but Council has done a thorough process of consultation, needs to respect that process and make sure that both the sporting community, the users of the park and the residents live around it have the opportunity to come together and enjoy what has been enjoyed now for 150 years. So Mr Mayor I believe these amendments are appropriate and should be incorporated within the plan and our community I think and the area will be much better for it. Thank you Councillor Williams.

text: Absolutely, you can. And I'll go back to Councillor Myles for an opportunity to reply. So go ahead.

speaker: elizabethkrassoi
text: Councillor Myles, you've spoken to the motion last night. It was, yep, okay, thank you. So it has been a long process, this plan of management. I've watched it, a very long process back in 2013 to 15 as a resident. And I thank the previous council for all the work they did on that plan of management. And this amended plan of management has also been quite long. But I just wanted to read a little bit about the introduction to the plan of management, just a couple of points on there that really resonate with me. I received quite a few emails over the last months, many months, since the plan was put on public exhibition in October. And I just got the feeling that perhaps some people were forming their opinions and giving their feedback based on things that they'd heard or been told or been asked to do, rather than actually what's written in this document, or without the benefit of knowing all the other things that are going on in this document. It's such an important document that we councillors are voting on tonight. So I'm just going to run through a few dot points in the introduction that I think should resonate for the whole community. Boronia Park, it protects three endangered ecological communities and provides a valuable habitat for a range of native animals, including several threatened species. It's part of a regionally significant wildlife corridor linking Sydney Harbour and the Lane It's listed as a heritage item in Schedule 5 of Council's Local Environmental Plan and includes several items of Aboriginal cultural heritage, significance and European historic heritage value. It provides three full-size sports fields. It's been a venue for rugby for over 100 years and includes the historic Grandstand and Oval. It's been a venue for rugby for over 100 years. and includes the historic Grandstand and Oval. It includes a cricket pitch and three high-standard lockable cricket nets, netball courts as well, junior playgrounds and a mixed-age playground. There's a couple of other points. It's traversed by the Great North Walk and it offers a choice of internal bushland walking tracks and a range of scattered park and picnic furniture. It's a popular venue for personal trainers, fitness groups, dog walkers, other small commercial group activities and services and it's an important scenic and visual element for both the local streetscape as well as views to and from the area. I love this introduction which then goes on to a plan of management that is very thick, many pages long and the management plan is built around all of those uses and needs and the things that we as a community value in Hunters Hill and I'm very proud to be on this council that's overseeing the amendments to it and ensuring the security of that area for future generations. It's why in the amendment just put by Councillor Sanderson I support the slightly smaller size, slightly smaller and significantly larger than some of the proposed suggested sizes for venues that have been put to council recently. The reason I support a smaller size is because I've seen comparable venues of 525 square metres and they don't fit with the values of the community that we've built this plan around based on their feedback, based on the history of the park and all of the needs that the park will be meeting. A 450 square metre site for a facility that the whole community can use is reasonable and it speaks to any architect or designer to say that this is what we in Hunters Hill want to fit in with our heritage, with our community and with our values and with that brief an architect will come up with something beautiful that our community will love and use well for many years to come. That said Hunters Hill is not a chocolate factory and if anyone remembers the Willy Wonka movie that I saw as a kid there used to be a line in it that said nobody ever goes in and nobody ever comes out. Well that's wrong. I for example use Wright Aquatic Centre, I use Lane Cove Swimming Pool, my son about 17 years ago played rugby at Hunters Hill Oval and at all the ovals in our neighbouring suburbs. I value all our neighbours and our whole northern region and I want them to value us as well. This is a premier park in every way for Hunters Hill. I'm really proud of the plan of management and I'm grateful to the general manager, the council officers and all the consultants who have endured a lengthy process of extensive transparent community consultation to build this report. Which brings me to the final thank you which is to our community who have engaged tooth and nail to make sure that this park that we all love services the needs of everyone and I think it's a fine, fine plan of management and we should all be very proud of it. It secures for our current and future generations a really valuable playground. It's also reviewable in just a few more years and so I wish it well to the future councillors who will be sitting here reviewing it down the track feeling proud of the park we've preserved for our whole community. Are you done?

speaker: markbennett
text: I am. Okay, so we seem to have almost reached the end. It's moved by Councillor Miles, seconded by Councillor Collins. You've spoken in favour of the motion, the amended motion. So, Councillor Miles, do you wish to have a final say on this, write a reply?

speaker: zacmiles
text: Yeah, I will, Mr Mayor. Only to say and thank you, Councillor Cressworth, that sentiment is obviously what this process is all about. Just to say that things shouldn't be lost in the plan. We do tend to get caught up in—we've tended to get caught up in a number of the sort of big ticket items but there are a whole lot of things if you go through the body of the plan itself that that go to the preservation of the park and its role in our community and I agree with you, Mr Mayor, that this is a regional facility and there's not many parks of this—it's a unique park in our part of Sydney, it's our premier park. This is step one in many respects for a lot of things that are going to be implemented as part of this plan in Boronia Park. For those that have concerns about the facility, the community facility that's being proposed, there's going to be another fairly exhaustive process which people will need to participate in and at the end of the day, we want to build something as a Council that services not just the clubs and not just Brainy Park Public School, the Humberfield Clubs but everyone in the community and that really is what the aim is here. There were assertions made during the course of this process that it was a yin and a yang and one group's getting everything and other groups are getting nothing. At the end of the day, I think with the carrying through of the passage of this draft plan into the actual plan of management, we need to make the process from now on as collaborative as possible because at the end of the day, the community facility that will be being constructed has to be something that is useful for all of our citizens and not just of Hunters Hill but of the broader region. It's a really exciting thing for me. I've been involved in this process since I first got on Council eight years ago and finally for the club, some people have been talking about this improvement in their facilities for some 30 years. I know that the Ravens are excited about the prospect of not having to call a year off and store it at home. I think that it's a good first step but it is just that. There is going to be a design process, an implementation process and a construction process after this. I think that we need to be as collaborative and make sure that people are as engaged as they possibly can be as we move forward because this will be probably one of the most significant things that we do as a Council. It is quite frankly the most significant project that I have been involved with in my eight years in Hunters Hill Council. I think this is a great first step. I'm excited about what we can deliver for the community here and I think that there's a long road ahead but there's one that we need to encourage everyone
